text: Pasteurised milk is boiled down under vacuum to about half solids, then sprayed as a fine mist into hot air, where the water leaves in a moment and a dry powder falls out. It keeps unchilled because it holds so little water.

steps.note: The concentrate's thickness is fixed before it is sprayed.
The milk is sprayed into hot air that enters at 200–220 °C and leaves at 75–80 °C.
